name: endfield
label: 终末地
description: 终末地 (Unity, Y-up): palette base from a per-instance constant-buffer record, camera from four consecutive view-projection rows.  This is the built-in solver the tool itself is fitted against.
notes: 终末地 (the built-in solver, `endfield`): per-instance palette base + view-projection rows.  This is the profile a run with no solver named falls back to, so it keeps the file name it has always had.  The engine is Unity, so the world is Y-up: `up_axis` turns +Y into Blender's +Z, and `left_handed` is OFF because that turn is already a proper rotation - (x, y, z) -> (x, -z, y) - and adding the Y mirror on top of it would both mirror the model and stand it on its head.  (It used to be `left_handed: true, up_axis: "z"`, which left every character lying along Blender's Y with its camera flipped; the silhouette check could not see either, because it renders with the very camera it grades.)
